name: Own it
definition: Be accountable for the outcome; don't wait for instructions. Bring solutions, not problems.

rows.under: Reports status. Treats the outcome as someone else's score.
rows.justRight: Is accountable for the outcome, not only the tasks. Stays with the work until the result is real.
rows.over: Claims every nearby outcome as theirs. Accountability becomes a land grab.

rows.situation: When the next step is not spelled out
rows.under: Waits for instructions. Does not move until someone assigns the work.
rows.justRight: Does not wait for instructions. Figures out the next step and takes it, then tells people what they did.
rows.over: Ignores the instructions that are already there. Invents a path that fights the plan.

rows.situation: Bringing a problem to the table
rows.under: Drops a problem and leaves. Expects someone else to solve it.
rows.justRight: Brings solutions, not only problems. Names the issue and a path through it.
rows.over: Insists on their solution before they have heard the problem. Solutions become a way to skip the discussion.

rows.situation: Work that has no clear owner
rows.under: Steps around it. If it is not on the list, it is not theirs.
rows.justRight: Picks up unowned work that blocks the outcome. Makes the ownership explicit so it does not drop again.
rows.over: Takes work that already has an owner. Creates a second plan in parallel.

rows.under: Explains why it was not their fault. The miss stays unowned.
rows.justRight: Owns the miss and the repair. Says what they will do differently.
rows.over: Owns the miss so loudly that the repair never starts. Apology replaces action.
